text:
anna-devex: Heads-up — noticed behavior mismatch between REST and JS SDK on the embeddings batch route. cURL to /v1/embeddings?allow_partial=true returns 200 with partials; SDK call with { allowPartial: true } throws 400.

mike-sdks: hmm. repro steps + minimal code? which SDK version?

anna-devex: SDK v1.8.1. Repro:
```
# REST
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?allow_partial=true" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"model":"tiny-embed","inputs":["a","b","c"]}'
```

and JS: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.TOKEN });
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'tiny-embed', inputs: ['a','b','c'], allowPartial: true });
```

REST returns 200 w/ partial vectors for failing inputs; SDK returns 400: "unknown parameter: allowPartial".

jess-samples: our quickstart sample app hits this in CI when we feed a mixed-length batch — blocks onboarding. :grimacing:

rachel-api: For historical context we renamed the query parameter on the API from `allow_partial` -> `allow_partial` (snake) to keep REST consistent; server accepts both snake and camel in query, but the JS SDK's request builder flattens body params to snake and filters unknown keys for the JSON body. Sounds like SDK is only allowing `allow_partial` in body but you're passing `allowPartial` in options so it gets rejected.

mike-sdks: thanks. I think two problems: 1) param normalization mapping is inconsistent between query vs body; 2) retry semantics differ when server responds with 499/429 vs 502. Is the SDK supposed to surface the partials on 200 but not treat 4xx as retriable?

sam-platform: FYI sample app expects partials as a feature flag when model is spotty; if SDK blocks with 400 we can't fall back to per-item requests. This increases cost.

mike-sdks: I'll patch param mapping to accept camelCase -> snake_case aliases for known flags and ensure the embeddings wrapper sends allow_partial in query if present. Also will add a test that compares REST curl vs SDK call for the batch endpoint.

anna-devex: also noticed retry header handling: REST returns `Retry-After` on 429, but SDK is only honoring `x-retry-after-ms` and not the standard header — causing faster-than-recommended retries. Seen some 429 storming in staging.

rachel-api: We started emitting both headers to help older clients, but clients should respect `Retry-After` if present. Looks like the JS SDK's retry policy is legacy.

mike-sdks: good catch. I'll align to `Retry-After` precedence and fall back to x-retry-after-ms. Plan: update request pipeline to copy response headers into the retry module, add mapping, and add a deterministic backoff test.

deploy-bot: New patch branch opened: fix/sdk-allow_partial-and-retry-headers (#2418) by mike-sdks — CI started.

jess-samples: thanks — once merged I'll update the quickstart and rerun CI. Any chance we can have a small note in the SDK changelog so customers don't get hit by this?

mike-sdks: yes, will add a CHANGELOG entry and a short migration note: "If you previously relied on camelCase flags in the JS SDK, v1.8.2+ will accept both camelCase and snake_case and will honor standard Retry-After headers."

anna-devex: awesome. One more ask — can we add a small integration test in samples that runs a quick curl vs SDK compare for shape-only (status + keys) on key endpoints (embeddings/generate)? Caught a bunch of silent drift before.

mike-sdks: +1. I'll add a lightweight smoke test in samples/ci that runs both paths.

rachel-api: will also add a short server-side compatibility test to ensure both header names are present until next major.

sam-platform: deploying the sample app canary after the fix. thanks team :raised_hands:
